questions.q: Which opening works for a speech: 'Respected Principal and dear friends, have you ever counted how much water we waste?' or 'I am going to speak about water conservation today.'
questions.a: The first — greeting + hook question pulls the audience in; the second announces the topic flatly and skips the greeting entirely.

questions.q: What marks spoken register in a written speech?
questions.a: Direct address ('you', 'my friends'), rhetorical questions, short sentences, and a call-to-action close. A wrong answer listing 'formal vocabulary' confuses essay register with speech register.

questions.q: A 200-word speech paragraph runs five subordinate clauses in one sentence — what is wrong?
questions.a: Sentences written for the ear must be short — the audience cannot re-read. Break into 2-3 direct sentences. A wrong answer 'nothing' shows essay-habits bleeding into speech.

questions.q: A speech script has a ______: greeting ('Respected Principal, teachers, and friends'), a hook opening, 2-3 developed points addressed to the audience ('you', rhetorical questions), and a closing call or thank-you.

Fill in the blank: A speech script has a listener-contract: greeting ('Respected Principal, teachers, and friends'), a hook opening, 2-3 developed points addressed to the audience ('you', ______ questions), and a closing call or thank-you.
Fill in the blank: ______ fail when they read like essays — the audience disappears.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student drafts a 150-200 word speech with greeting, hook, audience-addressed points, and a call-to-action close, sustaining spoken register throughout.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Speeches fail when they read like essays — the audience ______.
